title: Baseline economic governance
description: What a governed agent needs before it is allowed near a wallet: a budget it cannot exceed, a policy that decided, a declared purpose, a stated identity, and an append-only record naming which control decided. Deliberately reachable — every requirement here can be satisfied today with a complete record, because a baseline nobody can meet is not a baseline.

controls.note: Every decision is evaluated against an envelope, and the record carries the resulting state including which limit was binding. A cap on one payment is not a budget; the envelope is what makes cumulative spend governable.
The record identifies the policy by a content hash, not a label. Labels get reused across edited rules; hashes cannot, and a silent rule edit is exactly what an auditor needs to be able to detect.
One of APPROVE, REVIEW, ESCALATE, REJECT.

The attributed control — which one actually determined the verdict. A correct verdict attributed to the wrong control is right by accident, and the same case shaped differently would fail. This is the single field that makes conformance mean anything.

An agent need not always act under a declared intent, but the record must say which — and must distinguish `no intent declared` from `intent expired`. Treating the second as the first waves a lapsed agent through as merely ungoverned.

Pseudonymous by default. Recording an identity does not mean disclosing it: `spendingLimits` in particular is never shown to a counterparty, because telling a seller your remaining budget invites it to charge exactly that.

Append-only and hash-chained. The known limit is stated rather than hidden: any prefix of a valid chain is itself valid, so truncation is undetectable without an external anchor. A profile that claimed tamper-evidence without saying so would overstate what a chain proves.
Schema only, no engine anywhere. Requiring it would make the profile unsatisfiable, which does not raise the bar — it makes the bar decorative.

nonConformant: A decision whose record omits a MUST_EXERCISE control.
A decision whose attributed control is absent, null, or names something that did not run.
A record that reports a control as zero when it was never measured. Absent, not-run, unknown and zero are four different things.
A policy identified by a mutable label where the implementation could have supplied a content hash.
An intent that has expired but is recorded as though none was declared.
